title: Design LRU Cache
contract: Operations [0,key,value] put; [1,key,0] get and refresh recency. Return get results, −1 for missing. Capacity is nonnegative.
brute: List<int[]> cache=new ArrayList<>();List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int[] op:ops){int found=-1;for(int i=0;i<cache.size();i++)if(cache.get(i)[0]==op[1]){found=i;break;}int[] entry=found<0?null:cache.remove(found);if(op[0]==1){out.add(entry==null?-1:entry[1]);if(entry!=null)cache.add(entry);}else if(capacity>0){cache.add(new int[]{op[1],op[2]});if(cache.size()>capacity)cache.remove(0);}emit("Scan keys and move a hit to most recent","cache",cache.toArray(new int[0][]),"answers",out);}return out;
optimal: LinkedHashMap<Integer,Integer> cache=new LinkedHashMap<>(16,0.75f,true);List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int[] op:ops){if(op[0]==1)out.add(cache.getOrDefault(op[1],-1));else if(capacity>0){cache.put(op[1],op[2]);if(cache.size()>capacity){Integer eldest=cache.keySet().iterator().next();cache.remove(eldest);}}emit("Hash lookup plus access-order linked entries","cache",cache,"answers",out);}return out;
reasoning: A recency list can implement the contract, but locating a key takes linear time.
Access-order LinkedHashMap combines hash lookup with linked ordering, the same key idea as a HashMap plus custom doubly linked list.
Reads and writes refresh recency; evict the eldest after exceeding capacity. Capacity zero stores nothing. This single-threaded design is not a concurrent cache.
